buildings.n: Kapel Onze-Lieve-Vrouw met de open hand

gateSources.Brustempoort: Onroerend Erfgoed protection decision 2025 (Luikerstraat / Naamsevest): the only surviving remains
gateSources.Clockempoort: inventory 140054 mentions the Clockempoort at the Sluisberg; position by the road east (uncertain)
gateSources.Stapelpoort: name from the Stapelstraat; position uncertain
gateSources.Kortenbospoort: name from the road to Kortenbos; uncertain
gateSources.Tiensepoort: road to Tienen on Ferraris; name uncertain

walls.source: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Sint-Truiden' (https://id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140054)
walls.note: Sint-Truiden stone town wall (from 1129) with five gates, standing in 1650 and blown up by Louis XIV's troops in 1675; its line survives as the tree-lined vesten. Traced from the octagonal moat on the Ferraris map (1777). Gate names other than the Brustempoort are not verified for 1650.

landmarks.y1650: Benedictine abbey founded 7th c., lord of half the town; its Romanesque abbey church and tower (11th c.) stood until the abbey was sold after 1794; the tower survives.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Sint-Truiden' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140054)

landmarks.y1650: Main parish church on the Grote Markt; its tower collapsed in 1668 (after 1650), so in 1650 the old tower stood (height not verified).
Cloth hall of the 14th c. on the market; the belfry tower was rebuilt in 1606 on the old base and is on the UNESCO list of belfries. The present town hall front is 18th c.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Sint-Truiden' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140054); UNESCO 'Belfries of Belgium and France'

landmarks.y1650: 13th-c. beguinage on abbey land, outside the walls to the north-east; church of 1265 with medieval murals.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Sint-Truiden' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140054)

landmarks.y1650: Franciscan church and friary (13th c.); part of the town wall survives in its garden.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Sint-Truiden' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140054)

landmarks.y1650: Gate towards Brustem and Liège; blown up in 1675, its underground remains are the oldest surviving town-wall fabric in Flanders.

ruler.land: Prinsbisdom Luik; joint lordship of the abbot of Sint-Truiden and the prince-bishop (inventory 140054)
ruler.name: Prinsbisdom Luik
ruler.sovereign: Prince-bishop Ferdinand of Bavaria (1612-50), then Maximilian Henry of Bavaria (elected 1650); neutral in the Franco-Spanish war (neutrality recognised by Spain only in 1654, see history-check F76)

overworld.note: coordinates are overworld metres: town-local metres (around origin) + centre; 1:1 scale inside radius
